# Ọṣọọsì, spelled the way the sources wrote it
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Ọṣọọsì** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Ọṣọọsì's mythology lives in praise-poetry and divination verse — the oríkì that greet him, the Ifá corpus that ranks him among the orisha, and the itan, the sacred stories of the diaspora houses that still tell of the one arrow. His praise-poems are the hunt distilled: the oríkì greet Ọ̀ṣọ́ọ̀sì as the hunter who kills with a single arrow — the archer whose patience is so complete that the forest gives him what it denies the noisy and the hasty.  In the Candomblé houses of Brazil the same idea opens his festivals: Oxóssi, rei das matas, king of the forest, the provider whose one shot feeds the whole town.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Ọṣọọsì
- **ASCII form:** ochosi
- **Meaning:** "The hunter — orisha of the hunt, the forest, and deliberate strategy (standard Yoruba Ọ̀ṣọ́ọ̀sì; Cuban Ochosi, Brazilian Oxóssi)"
- **Domain of influence:** Hunting, Forest, Justice
- **Pantheon:** Yoruba
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ọ̀ṣọ́ọ̀sì
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 171 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Ọṣọọsì** to *ochosi* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **i → ì** — Grave: low tone: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Ọṣọọsì** lives at [/sites/ochosi/](/sites/ochosi/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ochosi/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ochosi/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ochosi/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Ọṣọọsì** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Forestry, Conservation & Outdoor Industries** — Lord of the forest hunt; the wildwood is his shrine and his range.
- **Legal, Justice & Compliance** — The orisha of justice; the single arrow that finds the truth and clears the accused.
- **Sports, Fitness & Competition** — The archer who never wastes an arrow; the hunt as precision discipline.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Yoruba tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Nigerian Studies — The Orisha Myths](/texts/nigerian-studies/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
